entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] The Russians' entry is an evil, but...! If Sergei Lavrov, Russia's Foreign…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @ahmadzeidabad

The Russians' entry is an evil, but...! If Sergei Lavrov, Russia's Foreign Minister, is carrying a plan to end the war between America and Iran on his trip to Tehran, the country's decision-makers as a whole ought to welcome it with open arms. I personally had wished that the Russians would be kept out of this conflict and that Iran and America would find a reasonable and balanced path to resolve the hostility themselves. Now that the inability of the two main parties to the conflict to defuse the tension has become evident, the Russians' intervention can be considered an opportunity for diplomacy. The Russians' intervention is, of course, an evil, but compared to the recurrence of war, it is the lesser evil! Therefore, welcoming the lesser evil in the face of the greater evil is what sound reason demands—that is, if any trace of sound reason remains! #احمد_زیدآبادی@ahmadzeidabad

In the third decade of the 21st century, weapons have become so terrifying and destructive that the firing and use of any one of them destroys everything from civilians to all kinds of facilities and the environment, causing destruction and devastation on a vast scale! entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] This side and that side of the roof! One day a Moroccan journalist told me a…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @ahmadzeidabad

This side and that side of the roof! One day a Moroccan journalist told me a story about the advice the late King Hassan of Morocco gave to Mohammad Reza Shah. According to his account, King Hassan told the former Shah of Iran never to wage war against the traditions and culture accepted by society, because he would lose his power. Mohammad Reza Shah did not follow King Hassan's advice. Imagining that he had destroyed the armed and leftist groups and that with the enormous oil money he could satisfy all segments and classes and consolidate and secure his power, he set about confronting certain religious symbols, the most provocative of which was changing the calendar from Hijri to Shahanshahi! These very acts of carelessness and neglect became one of the most important reasons for his fall. At present, Ilham Aliyev, the President of Azerbaijan, has also taken a risk with the ban on hijab in girls' schools that could lead to instability or the undermining of his rule. Meanwhile, however, certain circles inside Iran have strongly protested that Masoud Pezeshkian's government has remained silent in the face of Aliyev's decision. Now let us suppose that the government of the Islamic Republic wants to protest to the government of the Republic of Azerbaijan — in what language should this protest be made so that Mr. Aliyev does not turn around and say to them: you yourselves have made hijab compulsory not only in schools but in your own society, and you condemn any kind of protest by foreign countries on this matter as interference in your internal affairs — on what basis have you protested our decision? Will the government or any of the governing institutions have a convincing answer for Aliyev? In this world, only someone who is himself a defender of matters being voluntary can protest against any kind of compulsory measure. In addition, if an extreme inclination toward that side of the roof carries with it the danger of falling, an excessive inclination toward this side of the roof is not very safe either! #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Did Vance really say that? Persian-language media inside and outside Iran have…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Did Vance really say that? Persian-language media inside and outside Iran have reported that JD Vance acknowledged his disagreement with Donald Trump over the Iran issue. It's a strange and unprecedented piece of news, and it doesn't square with diplomatic etiquette in America. Vance may indeed disagree with Trump over war or Iran, but airing it before the media is unusual in every respect. So it seems to me that the media made an error in the initial drafting of this news. The Persian text of the report also doesn't indicate that Vance was referring to his disagreement with Trump. In my view, the pronoun in his sentence refers to Tucker Carlson, not to Trump. These days my internet access is limited and I can't verify this news, so the outlets that published it should look into it further. False and imprecise news, even in the field of foreign affairs, doesn't seem all that dangerous, but it is in fact very dangerous, because relying on such news leads to analyses of the kind Saeed Laylaz produces! Some people, in their capacity as "analysts," pay no attention whatsoever to the news as the primary data for any kind of commentary, and are themselves busy around the clock producing and distributing fake news and offering analysis based on it! It's this very group that has brought the country to this pass, and there is a fear that they will run it entirely into the ground! #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Negotiation as a tactic of war or a tool in the service of peace?…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Negotiation as a tactic of war or a tool in the service of peace? Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, has repeated for the umpteenth time that "we fight and we negotiate." Yes. There is no contradiction between war and negotiation such that one must choose one or the other. But what is meant by negotiation? Is negotiation a tool for achieving peace and ending hostility? Or is it a tactic to create opportunities and buy time to equip oneself in order to be better prepared to continue the war? If the second meaning is intended, then framing the war-negotiation duality is pointless, because in that case negotiation amounts to nothing more than a tactic of war. But if what is meant by negotiation is ending the war and achieving peace, then the war-peace duality is a more logical substitute for the war-negotiation duality. War and peace, however, unlike war and negotiation, are contradictory and cannot be reconciled; therefore, one must inevitably choose between them. In my view, our country has now reached a point where it must inevitably choose between war and peace. Mr. Qalibaf, as the head of Iran's negotiating team, is obliged to confront public opinion on this matter with greater candor and courage. It is the responsibility of Mr. Qalibaf and other officials who speak on this matter to give these terms conceptual clarity. Words and expressions without conceptual clarity are like balloons full of air and serve more for entertainment than for conveying a message and clarifying a goal! The political atmosphere of our country has become so bloated from the sheer volume and accumulation of undefined words that everyone is bewildered and dazed! #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad
